claim: Altered leptin signaling in utero may predispose the fetus to leptin resistance.
source: Altered leptin signaling in utero may predispose the fetus to leptin resistance and possibly be the link to the high rates of fetal overgrowth, childhood obesity, and the risk of developing asthma later in childhood (Yura et al., 2005; Stefaniak et al., 2019; Castro-Rodriguez et al., 2020)
evidence: Supported by citations to Yura et al., 2005, Stefaniak et al., 2019, and Castro-Rodriguez et al., 2020

claim: Leptin has been shown to stimulate monocyte activation and differentiation.
source: Furthermore, leptin has been shown to stimulate monocyte activation and differentiation (Santos-Alvarez et al., 1999)
evidence: Supported by citation to Santos-Alvarez et al., 1999

claim: Monocytes and macrophages are some of the earliest immune cells to develop with the first wave originating from late yolk-sac-derived erythromyeloid progenitors and fetal liver.
source: Indeed, monocytes and macrophages are some of the earliest immune cells to develop with the first wave originating from late yolk-sac-derived erythromyeloid progenitors and fetal liver (Wolf et al., 2019)
evidence: Supported by citation to Wolf et al., 2019

claim: A recent study demonstrated a proinflammatory phenotype within bone marrow macrophages of GD130 fetuses born to dams on WSD.
source: A recent study demonstrated a proinflammatory phenotype within bone marrow macrophages of GD130 fetuses born to dams on WSD (Sureshchandra et al., 2022)
evidence: Supported by citation to Sureshchandra et al., 2022

claim: The heightened maternal inflammatory milieu associated with obesity/WSD during critical windows of fetal immune ontogeny may skew the maturation of immune cells toward a regulatory state.
source: The heightened maternal inflammatory milieu associated with obesity/WSD during critical windows of fetal immune ontogeny may skew the maturation of immune cells toward a regulatory state, perhaps a protective adaptation to limit fetal inflammation.
evidence: Based on inference from experimental data and speculation about mechanisms

claim: Regulatory skewing contributes to less-than-ideal responses against pathogens in offspring of obese mothers.
source: However, this regulatory skewing also contributes to less-than-ideal responses against pathogens, as observed in both animal models and human studies.
evidence: Based on inference from experimental data presented in the study

claim: UCB monocytes from babies born to mothers with obesity are transcriptionally primed to respond poorly to ex vivo stimulation signals.
source: We next asked if cord blood monocyte subsets were transcriptionally primed to respond poorly to ex vivo stimulation signals.
evidence: Inferred from scRNA-seq data showing reduced inflammatory signatures and poor responses to stimulation

claim: UCB monocytes from babies born to mothers with obesity are predisposed toward a refractory/immune-tolerant state.
source: Importantly, these data indicate that UCB monocytes from babies born to mothers with obesity are predisposed toward a refractory/immune-tolerant state.
evidence: Based on inference from multiple experimental observations including reduced inflammatory responses and increased phagocytosis

claim: UCB monocytes from babies born to mothers with obesity display an unbalanced response to M1 and M2 polarizing stimuli mediated by alteration in methylation patterns at key promoter regions.
source: A similar phenotype was recorded in a previous study where UCB monocyte-derived macrophages from mothers with obesity displayed an unbalanced response to M1 and M2 polarizing stimuli mediated by alteration in methylation patterns at key promoter regions (Cifuentes-Zúñiga et al., 2017)
evidence: Supported by citation to Cifuentes-Zúñiga et al., 2017

claim: Lower transcript levels of IFNA could contribute to poor induction of ISG following RSV infection.
source: It is possible that lower transcript levels of IFNA could contribute to this outcome.
evidence: Based on speculation about mechanisms underlying observed data

claim: Epigenetic or signaling defects likely contribute to dampened ability of UCB monocytes to respond to IFNɑ/IFNβ.
source: However, other factors such as epigenetic or signaling defects are likely to contribute given the dampened ability of the cells to respond to IFNɑ/IFNβ when supplied in vitro despite the comparable surface protein expression of IFNAR1.
evidence: Based on inference from experimental data showing comparable receptor expression but reduced response

claim: UCB monocytes from obese group are unable to effectively integrate signals downstream of PRR.
source: Collectively, these findings suggest that UCB monocytes from obese group are unable to effectively integrate signals downstream of PRR, which culminate into dysregulated opening of chromatin, nuclear translocation of transcription factors, and their binding to specific genomic loci.
evidence: Based on inference from multiple experimental observations including signaling, epigenetic, and transcriptional data

claim: Closed chromatin profiles at baseline suggest that UCB monocytes from obese group are epigenetically poised to respond poorly to subsequent stimulation.
source: Closed chromatin profiles at baseline suggest that these cells are epigenetically poised to respond poorly to subsequent stimulation.
evidence: Based on inference from ATAC-seq data showing reduced chromatin accessibility

claim: The lack of robust metabolic, epigenetic, and transcriptional response to stimulation provides evidence for mechanistic constraints contributing to innate immune tolerance.
source: Thus, the lack of robust metabolic, epigenetic, and transcriptional response to stimulation provides further evidence for mechanistic constraints contributing to innate immune tolerance.
evidence: Based on inference from multiple experimental observations

claim: Some epigenetic modifications may be inherited through alterations in gametes, but others may be in response to maternal inflammatory and nutritional cues.
source: Some of these epigenetic modifications may be inherited through alterations in gametes, but others may be in response to maternal inflammatory and nutritional cues (Li, 2018)
evidence: Supported by citation to Li, 2018 and speculation about mechanisms

claim: Both circulating monocytes and tissue-resident macrophages generated a dampened response strongly suggests that this programming occurs early during gestation.
source: More importantly, the fact that both circulating monocytes and tissue-resident macrophages generated a dampened response strongly suggests that this programming occurs early during gestation.
evidence: Based on inference from rhesus macaque data showing effects in both cell types

claim: The regulatory skewing may be a protective adaptation to limit fetal inflammation.
source: The heightened maternal inflammatory milieu associated with obesity/WSD during critical windows of fetal immune ontogeny may skew the maturation of immune cells toward a regulatory state, perhaps a protective adaptation to limit fetal inflammation.
evidence: Based on speculation about evolutionary/biological mechanisms
